reference.source: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology / endocrine genetics reference literature
clinicalPearls: A monogenic autoimmune disorder caused by mutations in the AIRE gene, which normally drives thymic negative selection of self-reactive T cells
Defined by the classic triad of chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis, hypoparathyroidism and primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison disease), with two of the three needed for diagnosis
Candidiasis usually appears first in childhood, followed by hypoparathyroidism and then adrenal failure
A wide range of additional autoimmune features may develop, including hypogonadism, type 1 diabetes, autoimmune hepatitis, pernicious anaemia, alopecia and vitiligo
Ectodermal features such as enamel hypoplasia, nail dystrophy and keratopathy support the diagnosis
High-titre neutralising autoantibodies against type-1 interferons and interleukin-17/22 are characteristic and underlie susceptibility to candidiasis
Because new component disorders emerge over years, lifelong surveillance for evolving endocrine and non-endocrine autoimmunity is essential
reference.pathophysiology: APS-1 results from loss-of-function mutations in the autoimmune regulator (AIRE) gene, which controls expression of tissue-specific self-antigens in thymic medullary epithelial cells. Defective AIRE impairs negative selection of autoreactive T cells, allowing escape of lymphocytes that attack multiple endocrine and non-endocrine tissues. The resulting organ-specific autoimmunity destroys the parathyroid glands and adrenal cortex among others, while neutralising autoantibodies against type-1 interferons and Th17 cytokines compromise mucosal antifungal immunity, explaining the characteristic chronic candidiasis.
additionalDifferentials: Isolated chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis from other immune defects
additionalInvestigations: AIRE gene sequencing to confirm the diagnosis
Calcium, phosphate and parathyroid hormone for hypoparathyroidism
Morning cortisol with ACTH stimulation and adrenal autoantibodies for Addison disease
Autoantibody panel including anti-interferon antibodies and organ-specific antibodies
Screening for additional components: thyroid, gonadal and glucose testing, liver enzymes and full blood count
Assessment of ectodermal features including dental and ophthalmic review
redFlags: Adrenal crisis from unrecognised or intercurrent-stress-precipitated adrenal insufficiency
Symptomatic hypocalcaemia with tetany, laryngospasm or seizures
Invasive or oesophageal candidiasis, or squamous carcinoma arising in chronic candidiasis
reference.prognosis: With hormone replacement and antifungal treatment most patients survive into adulthood, but the disease is lifelong and mortality is driven by adrenal crises, severe hypocalcaemia, fulminant hepatitis and complications of chronic candidiasis.
pitfalls: Managing each component in isolation and failing to anticipate emerging new autoimmune disorders
Overlooking coexisting adrenal insufficiency when treating hypoparathyroidism, risking crisis
Attributing recurrent candidiasis to simple infection rather than the underlying immune defect
Missing autoimmune hepatitis or other non-endocrine components during follow-up
Not offering genetic counselling and family screening
references: Reference literature on AIRE and autoimmune polyendocrine syndromes
management: Lifelong glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid replacement for primary adrenal insufficiency
Calcium supplementation with an activated vitamin D analogue such as alfacalcidol or calcitriol for hypoparathyroidism
Suppressive azole antifungal therapy for chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis, with vigilance for azole resistance and oral squamous carcinoma
Establish and treat adrenal insufficiency before introducing thyroxine or other therapies that raise metabolic demand
Immunosuppression for autoimmune hepatitis and replacement therapy for other emerging components such as hypogonadism and type 1 diabetes
Emergency treatment of adrenal crisis and of symptomatic hypocalcaemia with parenteral calcium
Lifelong surveillance for new endocrine and non-endocrine components, including liver enzymes for fulminant hepatitis
Genetic counselling and family screening given autosomal recessive AIRE inheritance, within endocrinology-led multidisciplinary care
